lines.text: That night, the great hall of Greyhollow held the strangest war council in the history of Aldmere. A one-armed steward. A hunter. A blacksmith. A knight who had been sober for almost a year. A spy. And a zero.
A Measurer's lens reads rings at a glance. Any one of those twelve can look at a farmer and see exactly what is inside him.
So let them look. We're farmers.
Farmers have one ring. You have four. Your blacksmith has four. In this village, a child carrying water has three.
Is three a lot?
Three is a knight, lad.
There were only three choices. I made myself say them out loud.
We could run.
Then everything breaks, my lord. You heard her. Leave your people, and whatever you gave them fades. Leave the land, and the frost comes back.
We could fight.
Twelve Measurers with the Grand Measurer's seal. Lay one finger on them and it's treason. And next spring, the king's whole army comes north.
Then we hide.
Hide a hundred and twelve people? Where?
Right here. In plain sight.
Before you plan anything, my lord, look at that lamp.
Tobin made it the week you arrived. The first lamp of rimeglass in Greyhollow. It has grown brighter every single month since. No one has ever added a drop of oil.
I thought I was just very good at lamps.
That light is your Root. Your bond with this land. The deeper it goes, the stronger your people can grow. Bram is at five because your Root allows five. And not one ring higher.
So that was it. Every roof I fixed. Every field I drained. Every debt I paid. It had all been going into that little lamp.
Ilse. Can I ask you something? You came here to find me. You've known for months. Why didn't you report me?
I was going to. I had the letter written.
Then you fixed the mill.
The mill? That's it?
I have measured a thousand noble children, my lord. Not one of them ever asked what was wrong with a peasant's mill.
After she left, I went up on the wall. She had said I could feel them. That the cold I had felt all winter was them.
So I closed my eyes, and for the first time in my life, I tried to feel the cold on purpose.
At first, nothing. Then, one by one, I felt them. Thin threads of cold, running out from me into the dark. A hundred and twelve of them.
One was Tobin, snoring. One was a little girl with a fever. One was Bram, still awake, sitting by the gate.
And one, the thickest and warmest of all, was lying on my feet.
Two days.
Two days, to make a hundred and twelve people look like nobody at all.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter sixteen, coming soon.
